title: Draft the email + a reusable notice
goal: Make a real parent email and a reusable notice template with AI — described safely, edited by you.

blocks.title: Describe it once, reuse it forever
blocks.body:
Let's make two things you'll actually use: a warm email for the parent in front of you today, and a notice template you can reuse every time a similar situation comes up.

Remember the one rule — describe the situation without naming the child. You bring the situation and the tone; AI brings the calm first draft; you stay the editor who sends it.

blocks.brief: Before we generate anything, write the short brief you'd hand AI. In 2–3 lines, describe the situation, the tone you want, and what you hope the parent does next — WITHOUT any student name or private detail. Example shape: "A student in my class has been missing homework. I want a warm, non-blaming note that invites the parent to a quick chat."
rubric: Describes the situation without naming the student or any private detail (health, family, marks-with-names)
Names the tone you want (e.g. warm, reassuring, firm-but-kind)
States the outcome — what you hope the parent does next
Reads like a note you'd actually send after a quick edit

blocks.scaffold: Draft a warm, clear {{artifact}} to parents about [situation] for a {{gradeBand}} {{subject}} class. Describe the situation without naming any student or private detail, keep the tone respectful and non-blaming, and end with one clear next step. Leave [blanks] I can fill in each time so I can reuse it.

blocks.question: How usable was the draft — would you send it, or reuse the template, after a quick edit of your own?
